ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the Bermuda AML/ATF framework. All directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized signatories must be screened against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List as extended to Bermuda, and Bermuda's domestic sanctions list. PEPs require enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and source of funds verification, senior management approval, and continuous monitoring. Adverse media and negative-news screening must be performed at onboarding and on an ongoing risk-sensitive basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Companies Registry electronic portal, operated by the Registrar of Companies of Bermuda (https://www.gov.bm/companies-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Bermuda Exempted Company must be in English and rendered in Latin/Roman script. Non-English names require an approved Latin-script transliteration. Chinese-language characters are not accepted as part of the registered legal name but may be registered as a supplementary trade name. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' and must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant has 30 days from the written rejection to submit a reconsideration request or an amended name through the same registry portal. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may file an originating application in the Supreme Court of Bermuda for judicial review within 28 days of the final administrative refusal. Administrative reconsideration carries no separate registry filing fee; court filing fees and counsel fees are additional and follow the prevailing Civil Appeals Rules and Solicitors' Remuneration Order.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or post-office box is not permissible as the statutory registered office. The registered office must be a physical Bermuda street address, normally the office of a licensed registered agent, at which legal process and official communications may be served. For a no-code website builder, the registered agent's physical office is sufficient; a supplementary virtual or marketing address may be used for commercial correspondence but cannot replace the statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: the estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection of the no-code software business premises is below 5% per annum because no statutory operating license or regulated financial services activity is involved. The licensed registered agent's office has a materially higher inspection risk of approximately 20-30% per annum due to Bermuda Monetary Authority and Financial Intelligence Agency AML/CFT supervision.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda, as amended: Part II on incorporation, memorandum of association and bye-laws (including the statutory definitional provisions for 'exempted company'), together with the duties of the Registrar of Companies under that Act; Exchange Control Act 1972 and subsidiary regulations (non-resident designation through the Bermuda Monetary Authority); Business Licensing Act 2000 (Business Licence only when carrying on business in Bermuda); Economic Substance Act 2018 (periodic substance reporting for relevant activities); Personal Information Protection Act 2016 (privacy registration if processing the data of Bermuda residents).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda (Hamilton, Bermuda); registration is effected wholly through the Registry's statutory incorporation procedure, in practice conducted by a licensed corporate services provider.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form FE (Application for Registration of an Exempted Company) filed together with the executed Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws; the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by Bermuda law. An exempted company must have at least one issued share; the Memorandum must state an authorized share capital (commonly USD 12,000 or the equivalent for fee-banding), and no escrow, deposit, or capitalization requirement applies. The Bermuda Monetary Authority requires the company to be designated 'non-resident' where all shareholders are non-residents.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD MEETING RESOLUTION — BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT: RESOLVED, that the subscriptions be and are hereby approved; the subscribers be allotted and issued the shares indicated against their names, credited fully paid; and the Secretary be directed to file the statutory return of allotment with the Registrar of Companies. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be established at [Bermuda Address] c/o the licensed corporate services provider, appointed to maintain the statutory registers and records. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed Director and [Name] appointed Secretary, each to serve until replaced, and be authorized to open bank and payment-processor accounts and appoint professional advisers on behalf of the Company.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Office of the Tax Commissioner, Government of Bermuda — official tax administration portal: www.gov.bm; corporate registry and company/TIN records: Registrar of Companies, www.roc.gov.bm; Pillar Two/CIT administration under the Tax Administration Act 2024 is also run by the Ministry of Finance (Tax Commissioner). Bermuda is a self-governing British Overseas Territory: Her Majesty's Revenue & Customs (HMRC) has no administrative authority over Bermuda tax affairs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company is incorporated under the Companies Act 1981; the Registrar of Companies automatically issues a company registration number which functions as the statutory TIN. No VAT ID exists because Bermuda imposes no VAT/GST, and no VAT registration can be made domestically. For payroll tax, the company must register as an employer with the Office of the Tax Commissioner via www.gov.bm as soon as it compensates Bermuda-based employees (no minimum payroll threshold). For an in-scope MNE group (consolidated revenue ≥ EUR 750 million), a CIT TIN and e-filing account are obtained from the Ministry of Finance under the Tax Administration Act 2024 (for FY commencing on or after 1 January 2025). Non-financial entities such as a no-code website builder require no FATCA/CRS registration and no GIIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — exempted company status confers automatic statutory exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, corporation tax, and withholding/distribution taxes until at least 31 March 2035, pursuant to the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966. Territorial scope: only Bermuda-source payroll tax and customs duty on physical imports can apply; digital export revenue is tax-neutral. Entity-level taxation is absent for SMBs; the Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 (15% rate) applies exclusively to constituent entities of large MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million, which is out of scope for an ISIC 6201 low-code builder operating below that threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No election is required for the 1966 Tax Protection guarantee — it applies automatically to all exempted companies. Bermuda has no US-style check-the-box regime and no pass-through classification election under local law. For CIT Act 2023 in-scope groups only: election to apply transitional country-by-country reporting safe harbour, election for a local constituent entity to file on behalf of the group, and the Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (QDMTT) mechanism are available. No hybrid mismatch elections are relevant because there is no material income tax base for SMB exempted companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None — Bermuda levies no VAT, GST, or sales-and-use tax. The only indirect-type duties are customs/import duties under the Customs Tariff Act 1971 (on physical goods entering Bermuda), plus the employer-side Payroll Tax Act 1995 which is a direct payroll levy, not an indirect tax. Cross-border digital services supplied by a Bermuda exempted company (no-code website builder) are outside all Bermuda indirect taxes. Separately, UK VAT may arise for B2C digital services supplied to UK consumers under UK law (non-established supplier threshold GBP 8,818 per annum) — this is a UK tax obligation, not a Bermuda one.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — Bermuda has no VAT turnover threshold and no indirect-tax registration mechanism in BMD. Customs duty is transactional per import entry; no general importer registration threshold applies to a pure digital service exporter. The employer payroll tax registration is triggered simply by engaging any Bermuda-based employee, regardless of the total remuneration level. All export proceeds from visual web template and low-code SaaS subscriptions are entirely outside the Bermuda customs and payroll base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing mandate, digital stamping, or B2B transaction e-reporting exists in Bermuda. Physical imports/exports are cleared electronically through the Bermuda Customs Management System only for goods movements. Digital service invoices issued via Stripe Billing or Paddle require no government clearance, no API integration, and no sequence-number validation with the tax authority.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — with no VAT/GST in place, there is no 0% export rating to claim, no output VAT to discharge, and no input VAT pool to refund. Exports of no-code website builder services under ISIC 6201/NAICS 511210 are automatically outside Bermuda's taxation and are never subject to Bermuda duties. If the entity also exports physical hardware or media, the goods leave Bermuda without export duty; only an accurate customs export entry is needed. Consequently, the entire export revenue base is tax-neutral at the Bermuda level.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Pure digital services (no-code website builder): no mandatory documentation — no customs export declaration, no bill of lading, and no inward remittance certificate is required by Bermuda law

Physical goods exported from Bermuda (e.g., servers, pre-loaded media): Bermuda Customs Export Entry filed via the Bermuda Customs Management System, Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and Bill of Lading
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT export zero-rating fraud or clawback can arise because no VAT system exists. The residual compliance risks are: (i) Customs Tariff Act 1971 penalties, including significant statutory fines and forfeiture, for misdeclared physical exports or imports; (ii) Payroll Tax Act 1995 and Tax Administration Act 2024 interest and late-filing penalties if Bermuda employees are engaged without registration; (iii) for groups above the EUR 750 million threshold, Corporate Income Tax Act 2023 penalties on understated top-up tax and late filing, applicable only from tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2025. The Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 prevents retrospective imposition of income/capital taxes on SMB exempted companies, and Bermuda has no exchange-control legislation, so there is no statutory FX repatriation deadline and no remittance-based clawback whatsoever.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) — the de facto central bank and integrated financial services regulator for Bermuda, a British Overseas Territory under HM Treasury oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and free convertibility on both current and capital accounts. Bermuda abolished exchange controls via the Exchange Control (Repeal) Act 2005; the Bermudian dollar (BMD) operates under a currency-board-style arrangement at a fixed 1:1 parity with the US dollar, backed by USD reserves. No BMA approval is required for inbound/outbound investment, dividend declarations, profit remittance, intercompany loans, or liquidation distributions. Residual practical hurdles are limited to bank-level internal enhanced due diligence on high-risk counterparty jurisdictions, CRS/FATCA transparency classification, and documentary evidence of economic substance where profit is repatriated from a tax-exempt entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Bermuda imposes no statutory surrender, conversion, or retention restriction on export proceeds or any foreign-currency receipts. Receipts from payment service providers (Stripe Billing, Paddle) may be held indefinitely in USD, BMD, GBP, or EUR in any BMA-licensed account; no mandatory conversion into BMD exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium feasibility. FCA-regulated European EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Airwallex) generally decline direct onboarding of Bermuda-incorporated entities under internal offshore-jurisdiction policies absent a substantive UK branch or a genuine UK permanent establishment; entities with a UK-registered branch or a UK-resident director with strong banking history may obtain a GBP/EUR settlement account from select EMIs. The legally robust path is a dual-rail structure: a Bermuda main operating account at Butterfield/HSBC for USD/BMD settlement, supplemented by a UK EMI account only if a UK establishment is formally registered; direct EMI settlement of Stripe/Paddle receivables into Bermuda accounts is operationally acceptable only where the MoR payment provider permits payouts to Bermudian bank accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate. Bermuda banks require at least one director (or a locally appointed authorized signatory) to attend an in-person onboarding interview at the bank's premises in Hamilton, Bermuda, or at a recognized overseas office; HSBC Bermuda and Butterfield permit remote completion where the director appears in a live video interview with a compliance officer AND provides notarized and apostilled passport copies, original certified corporate documents, and a professional introducer letter from a Bermuda-licensed corporate services provider. A bank-to-bank reference letter with at least a three-year relationship history materially accelerates the waiver of the physical appearance requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore exempted-company status with zero domestic tax may trigger 'tax haven' enhanced due diligence (EDD) and heightened reputational screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Exemption under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966; BMA or Registrar of Companies registration evidence; FATF/CFATF membership confirmation via the UK; an economic substance position paper demonstrating core income-generating activities (CIGAs) performed in Bermuda or a qualifying jurisdiction, supported by the latest ESR return, payroll records, and a physical office lease if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity from nominee shareholders, trust arrangements, or multi-tier group structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial ownership register filed under the Companies Act 1981 (Bermuda), including percentages of ownership; signed declaration of trust or nominee acknowledgment; introduction letter from a licensed corporate services provider (CSP); group structure organogram ending at natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; source of wealth statements for each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or 'digital-only' revenue model without physical invoices may be treated as high-risk money-service-business or shell activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Merchant of Record agreements with Stripe Billing and Paddle; live website URLs, DNS records, and traffic evidence; master SaaS subscription terms; sub-processor and cloud infrastructure contracts; proforma income statements for 12 months; FATF-compliant AML risk self-assessment confirming low-risk software product classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows with UK parent or foreign founders lacking coherent tax-residency narrative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing account opening; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms; tax residence certificates for all directors and UBOs; low-risk intercompany services agreement and transfer-pricing documentation; auditor's or UK law firm's opinion confirming no permanent establishment exposure in the UK absent a UK branch.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No exchange-control authorization is required. Inbound equity injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the UK/global remitter using OECD BPM6 purpose code '611 – Direct Investment: Equity Capital'; the UK remitter's bank may additionally map this to a domestic outward-remittance purpose category such as 'Direct Investment' or 'Capital Contribution'. The Bermuda receiving bank (Butterfield/HSBC) will credit the USD/BMD capital account upon receipt of a board resolution, a share allotment form filed under the Companies Act 1981, and a source-of-funds statement from the remitting bank. The transfer should reference the entity's full legal name and account number; a scanned copy of the bank confirmation is sufficient for the BMA's ex-post supervisory framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pain.001 where the counterparty bank supports it) for vendor payments, contractor settlements, cloud-infrastructure charges, and profit repatriation. Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) are legally permissible but commercially irrelevant for a no-code SaaS builder because no physical goods are traded; standby letters of credit may be used solely as performance security in enterprise contracts. Daily merchant-settlement flows from Stripe Billing and Paddle are received via Card/ACH/SEPA/SWIFT according to each MoR agreement, swept into the Bermuda operating account, and then disbursed via MT103 netting cycles to optimize USD/BMD parity conversion costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contract (vanilla) with a BMA-licensed bank (Butterfield, HSBC Bermuda) to hedge USD/GBP and USD/EUR net revenue conversion — permitted without BMA approval and subject to standard ISDA or local master agreement documentation.

Cross-currency swap (USD to GBP or USD to EUR, fixed/floating legs) for cash-flow matching of cloud-infrastructure and contractor expenses — permissible under Bermuda law with board authorization and appropriate disclosure in financial statements.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for exotic pairs (e.g., BRL, CNH, INR) through a non-Bermuda licensed dealer — permitted where BMD/USD parity makes onshore forwards unnecessary; the BMD/USD pair itself requires no hedge because of the fixed 1:1 currency-board peg.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Commerce and Economic Development, Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of BMD 10 per day accruing from day 61; publication in the defaulting companies list; administrative strike-off by the Registrar following continued non-payment (typically after 90–120 days)

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory for exempted companies that are listed on a recognised stock exchange, licensed or registered under Bermuda's regulated activities regimes (e.g., insurance, banking, investment funds), or are subsidiaries of a consolidated group requiring audited accounts. An ordinary non-listed, non-regulated exempted company may waive the audit appointment by shareholder special resolution; no financial statements are publicly filed with the Registrar.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or US GAAP, as adopted by the board of directors; Bermuda does not prescribe a separate local GAAP for exempted companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Beneficial Ownership Act 2017 and Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations, the exempted company must maintain a beneficial ownership register at its registered office and provide access to the Registrar and the Financial Information Group upon request. No separate public UBO annual filing is made; however, the annual return must confirm the current shareholders and controlling parties, and any share transfer or change of beneficial owner must be recorded in the statutory registers and, where applicable, confirmed to the Registrar within the relevant calendar year.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Bermuda imposes no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or other distributions for exempted companies. Companies may apply for a tax assurance certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, guaranteeing no future Bermuda tax on profits, dividends, or capital until 31 March 2035.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return for Exempted Companies (Form RC4/RC5/RC6 as applicable) filed via the Bermuda Registrar of Companies electronic filing portal (Bermuda Corporate Registry eServices).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due by 31 January following the calendar year end, or the anniversary of incorporation if an alternative filing date is elected. A company with a non-calendar fiscal year may apply for a different filing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, company number, registered office address in Bermuda, incorporation date, and principal place of business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Bermuda registered office address exactly; do not list overseas operational headquarters as registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names, residential addresses, appointment dates, and nationality of all directors and the company secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-Bermudian directors must provide a Bermuda care-of address; residential addresses may be filed on a confidential basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital, issued share capital, share classes, consideration paid, and shareholders holding 5% or more of any class.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State issued shares to non-resident owners and the currency. For non-cash consideration, attach a description and valuation method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of exempted company's principal business activity and whether it will conduct business in Bermuda.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State 'No business conducted in Bermuda; commercial operations conducted entirely outside Bermuda.' Use ISIC Rev.4 code 6201.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration signed by a director or authorized representative attesting to the accuracy of the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident director may sign electronically; include the director's name and capacity. If filed by an agent, attach a board resolution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of BD$100 plus BD$10 per day, up to a maximum of BD$1,000. Failure may also result in the company being struck off and dissolved.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Bermuda has no comprehensive double taxation agreement with the UK or most jurisdictions. Relief from foreign withholding taxes is not available under a Bermuda DTA. Instead, foreign tax authorities may grant unilateral relief or domestic law exemption. A company needing proof of tax residency may obtain a Certificate of Resident Status / Tax Exemption Letter from the Bermuda Registrar of Companies or Ministry of Finance by submitting Form 1A and supporting evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Bermuda statutory WHT on royalties and interest is 0%. In the source jurisdiction (e.g., UK), UK domestic WHT may apply to software royalties paid from UK sources at 20% unless the UK recipient is within the charge to UK corporation tax. UK interest withholding may apply at 20% unless the UK corporate exemption applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Bermuda does not impose transfer pricing documentation requirements under local tax law because there is no corporate income tax. However, multinational groups with UK or other foreign operations must maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation if their foreign filing thresholds apply (e.g., UK Local File threshold typically applies where UK group revenue exceeds £200 million and related-party transactions exceed £20 million; intercompany transactions exceeding £5 million may require documentation). As a practical benchmark, prepare documentation where annual intercompany royalties or service fees exceed US$1 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Bermuda's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to exempted companies carrying on relevant activities, including IP holding, distribution and service centers, financing and leasing, and pure holding business. A no-code website builder must demonstrate adequate economic substance in Bermuda if it is a relevant entity not tax resident elsewhere. If the company is tax resident in another jurisdiction, it must file an annual ESR Declaration confirming its foreign tax residence and provide a certificate of tax residence. Non-compliance carries substantial penalties and information exchange with foreign tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Carrying on a relevant activity without meeting the economic substance test, failing to file the annual Economic Substance Return or Declaration, or falsely claiming tax residence in another jurisdiction without supporting evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty of BD$10,000, plus BD$10,000 per additional day of non-compliance; separate penalties up to BD$5,000 plus BD$500 per day for documentation failures. The Registrar may issue compliance notices and ultimately strike the company off.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit non-compliance may be personally liable for civil penalties and, in cases of false declarations, imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to BD$50,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or file a beneficial ownership register, failure to report suspicious activity to the Bermuda Financial Intelligence Agency, or processing payments in violation of anti-money laundering obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to BD$50,000; late filing penalties up to BD$500 per day; accounts may be frozen or payment processors terminated. The Minister may revoke tax assurance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face personal fines up to BD$500,000 and imprisonment up to 20 years for money laundering. Civil asset recovery and travel bans may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Attributing business income to the Bermuda exempted company while controlling and executing the core revenue-generating activities in the UK or another jurisdiction, creating a permanent establishment or sham arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: HMRC may assess UK corporation tax at 25% on UK-attributable profits, plus late payment interest and penalties up to 100% of the tax liability for deliberate concealment. Follower notices and accelerated payment notices may be issued.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders may be prosecuted under the UK Criminal Finances Act 2017 for failure to prevent facilitation of tax evasion; unlimited fines and imprisonment up to 5 years. Director disqualification orders and veil-piercing by HMRC are possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a Bermuda registered agent and registered office, or failure to file the Annual Return and Economic Substance Declaration within statutory deadlines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalties of BD$100 plus BD$10 per day (maximum BD$1,000); company loses good standing and may be struck off after continued default.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for company debts incurred after striking off and may be disqualified from acting as directors in Bermuda.
